tapeLine: Friday 13 November: S&P 500 −0.4% (−30.73) to 7,561.67; Dow +0.1% (+50.46) to 52,347.55; Nasdaq Composite −0.91% (−229.82) to 25,136.27; Russell 2000 −0.3% to 2,790.49, per AP close reports dated 13 Nov. For the week: S&P 500 +2.5%, Nasdaq +2.3%, Dow +2.1%, Russell 2000 +1.3% (AP).
matters:
October PPI came in at +0.3% m/m against a +0.4% consensus, with the annual rate at 6.5%, the largest 12-month rise since November 2022 (BLS via CNBC, 13 Nov). Core PPI rose 0.3% m/m and 5% y/y (CNN, 13 Nov). The 10-year Treasury yield moved to about 5.15% Friday (CNBC, 13 Nov), and CNBC reported markets pricing at least a quarter-point Fed hike at the December meeting. Tech led Friday’s decline: the S&P 500 tech sector fell 1.7%, the worst of 11 sectors, and Nvidia fell about 2% (Kiplinger/Reuters, 13 Nov).

This week: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh speaks today at 12:00 ET; October retail sales Tuesday; Nvidia’s third-quarter results after Tuesday’s close, the first under interim CEO Colette Kress; October FOMC minutes Wednesday; Anthropic’s IPO is reported to price Wednesday 18 Nov with Nasdaq trading under ANT from Thursday 19 Nov, timing subject to change. Futures were lower early Monday, with CNBC showing Nasdaq-100 futures −0.79% and S&P 500 futures −0.25%.

calendar.event: Fed Chair Warsh, opening remarks, Productivity and Jobs Task Force conference (San Francisco)

alsoOnTape: 10-year Treasury yield about 5.15% on Friday, up roughly 5 bp on the day (CNBC and Forbes, 13 Nov). Brent crude settled $95.84 Friday per Yahoo Finance history; Investing.com shows $96.13, so treat it as mid-$95 to $96. Gold and VIX levels were not found with a clean dated source.
overnight: Latest confirmed close — Friday 13 November: S&P 500 7,561.67 (−0.4%); Nasdaq Composite 25,136.27 (−0.91%); Dow 52,347.55 (+0.1%). All three indexes finished the week higher (AP).

Futures — early Monday 16 Nov: Nasdaq-100 −0.79%, S&P 500 −0.25% (CNBC live updates); Reuters via MarketScreener described S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 futures as sliding as AI-linked stocks came under pressure ahead of Nvidia.

Nvidia — closed Friday at $162.85, down 12.7% for the week, per Investing.com’s week-ahead note dated 16 Nov; Reuters/Kiplinger put the weekly loss near 13%, its worst since April 2025. Shares were lower premarket Monday. Results come after Tuesday’s close; revenue consensus figures cited range from $108.73 billion to $109.1 billion and are not carried as a single number.
macro: PPI, October — final demand +0.3% m/m (consensus +0.4%), +6.5% y/y; core +0.3% m/m, +5% y/y. Food prices rose 1.3% on the month, the fastest since July 2022 (BLS via CNBC and CNN, 13 Nov).
Fed path — CNBC reported markets pricing at least a quarter-point hike at the December meeting after the October inflation data (13 Nov). Warsh speaks today; FOMC minutes Wednesday.

Anthropic IPO — preliminary range $70–$78 per Class A share on 825 million shares; pricing reported for 18 Nov and first Nasdaq trade 19 Nov under ANT, per secondary reports of the S-1 timetable announced 12 Nov. Valuation estimates in coverage conflict and are not carried.
flow: Breadth, dealer gamma, put-call and skew are paid data and are not on this page.

regime.tag: Indexes closed a strong week on a soft Friday; Nvidia earnings and the Anthropic listing make this an AI-heavy week with yields above 5%.
regime.sizing: PPI came in a tenth below consensus yet the 10-year still rose to about 5.15%; how equities trade AI news against that rate level is unresolved.

secondOrder: Friday’s PPI was softer than expected on the month, yet yields rose and the Dow was the only major index higher, while tech fell hardest. The week as a whole was the best since early August for all three indexes (CNBC), despite Nvidia’s roughly 13% weekly drop. That is an observation, not a forecast.

scorecard.text: The prior brief listed October PPI consensus at +0.4% m/m and +6.6% y/y, and said 6.6% would be the largest annual rise since November 2022. The print was +0.3% m/m and +6.5% y/y, still the largest since November 2022 (CNBC, 13 Nov). The consensus listing was accurate; the reading came in a tenth below on both measures.

The prior brief said Nvidia reports third-quarter earnings Tuesday 17 Nov under an interim CEO. Week-ahead previews dated 16 Nov confirm results after Tuesday’s close, with Colette Kress as interim CEO.

The prior brief said how a PPI reading above or below consensus would land was unresolved. It came in below, the 10-year rose to about 5.15% and the S&P 500 fell 0.4%. No direction was called, so there is nothing to grade right or wrong.
